record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: For the vacuum Einstein equations, prove a theorem saying that if an approximate metric g_e has Ricci curvature small in a suitable norm, then there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric g close to g_e in that norm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge 3$ (Riemannian or Lorentzian setting may be specified). The vacuum Einstein equations on $M$ are the equation $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ for the Ricci curvature of a metric $g$. Call a metric $g_e$ on $M$ an "approximate vacuum metric" if $\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)$ is small in some suitable function-space norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ on symmetric $(0,2)$-tensors (for example, a weighted Hölder or Sobolev norm appropriate to the asymptotic geometry of $(M,g_e)$).

Problem. Formulate and prove a perturbation/stability theorem of the following form: there exist constants $\varepsilon>0$ and $C>0$, depending only on $(M,g_e)$ through controlled geometric quantities, such that whenever $g_e$ is an approximate vacuum metric with
$$\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)\|_X < \varepsilon,$$
there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric $g$ on $M$ (a solution of $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$) satisfying
$$\|g - g_e\|_X \le C\,\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)\|_X.$$

In particular, identify suitable norms $X$, geometric/analytic non-degeneracy hypotheses on the linearization of the Ricci operator (modulo diffeomorphism gauge) at $g_e$, and asymptotic conditions on $(M,g_e)$ under which such a quantitative existence-and-closeness statement holds.
artifact.status_search_result: No direct evidence was found that a general "approximate-implies-exact" theorem for Ricci-flat metrics, in the broad form requested, has been established. Partial results exist in specific settings (e.g., gluing constructions, asymptotically flat or asymptotically hyperbolic perturbation results, and stability theorems near non-degenerate Einstein metrics), but a general statement encompassing all relevant cases does not appear to be settled. Status is therefore marked unknown.

status_evidence.title: Ricci-flat manifold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Ricci-flat Lorentzian manifolds are solutions of Einstein's field equations in a vacuum with vanishing cosmological constant.
status_evidence.claim: Background: vacuum Einstein equations correspond to Ricci-flat metrics; no general perturbation theorem of the stated form is cited.

status_evidence.title: Einstein manifold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Einstein metrics solve the vacuum Einstein field equations with cosmological constant.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references describe stability only under specific non-degeneracy hypotheses, not a fully general theorem.
